audit_meta.title: Navis read-only forensic code audit
audit_meta.method: Static reading of implemented code and tracing execution paths from entry points. Documentation and planned architecture were not treated as evidence. The Core backend (~/Desktop/Backend) is NOT in scope; it was grepped read-only only to confirm whether a route the audited code calls actually exists. Deployment status comes from anonymous HTTP/DNS probes run on 2026-10-04.
constraints_honoured: No existing file in either repository was modified. This JSON is the only file created, as a new untracked file at the Devtool root.

No test suite, build or dev server was executed, because `npm test` builds dist/ and test runners write caches, which would modify the repos. Test counts below are static counts of test cases, not pass/fail results.
No authenticated call was made to any environment. Staging was probed anonymously only (expecting 401 for auth-gated routes).

status_vocabulary.production: Served from a public production host. NOTHING in either audited repo qualifies as of 2026-10-04.
status_vocabulary.staging: Deployed on https://staging-api.navislabs.in and confirmed by an anonymous probe or the public staging OpenAPI document.
status_vocabulary.working: Implemented end to end against the real Core, covered by unit tests, runs locally. Not deployed publicly.
status_vocabulary.mock: Returns fixtures, synthetic values, or a deliberate stub instead of real data.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Cross-session work-state continuity for Claude Code
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: `navis hook <SessionStart|UserPromptSubmit|PreCompact|SessionEnd>`, invoked by Claude Code hooks (wired locally in Devtool/.claude/settings.local.json) -> program.ts command 'hook' -> runHook (hook.ts:214) -> handle (hook.ts:356)
implementation_flow: Claude Code pipes a JSON payload on stdin; readHookInput/parseHookPayload (workstate/hooks.ts) extract the session id, prompt and cwd, and strip previously injected context.
deriveWorkIdentity (identity.ts:124) computes a stable work key from the canonicalised git remote and branch (or path) and derives per-session idempotency keys for tasks and runs.

SessionStart (hook.ts:384): Promise.all of loadCurrentWorkState (find the open task by work key, list runs, probe the latest outcome) and me(). It joins this session's run concurrently, and only if NAVIS_WORKSTATE_CONTEXT=1 does it also call POST /developer/context with tokenBudget 800.

renderRestoration (restore.ts:99) builds a block of at most 3,000 characters in priority order (work state, then organizational facts), wrapped in per-render random-nonce delimiters (restore.ts:212). Delimiter-shaped text from storage is defanged (restore.ts:239), and every absence is stated. Stdout is injected into the model's context.
UserPromptSubmit (hook.ts:585) opens the work stream once per session using ids cached in the local session file (~/.local/state/navis/workstate) and prints nothing.

PreCompact (hook.ts:681) merges the patch into the base checkpoint (checkpoint.ts:540), scrubs secrets (checkpoint.ts:846), and recordCheckpoint (service.ts:866) PUTs it as the run outcome with ifNewer:true. A 409 counts as stale and is skipped, not retried (service.ts:950), and the write is read back and verified (service.ts:989).
SessionEnd (hook.ts:850) writes a best-effort final checkpoint under a hard wall-clock budget.
Every failure path exits 0 with a stderr diagnostic, so a dead Core never blocks the developer's prompt.
evidence: hook.ts header: 'every failure ... resolves to exit 0 with a diagnostic on stderr and nothing on stdout'.
restore.ts:57 RESTORE_MAX_CHARS = 3000, sized from measured real checkpoints (comment cites 8/8 partial restores at 1500 on 2026-09-25).
service.ts:905 `ifNewer: true`; service.ts:950 isStaleWriteRefusal -> status 409; service.ts:933 verifyPersisted.

Live in this audit: this session's SessionStart hook printed 'NAVIS WORK CONTINUITY — NOT RESTORED: Navis could not be reached ... Do not treat this as no previous work', the designed degraded path, because Core :8000 was down.
~512 test cases in 19 files (service.test.ts 1,094 lines, restore.test.ts 908, checkpoint.test.ts 895, hook.test.ts 872, architecture.test.ts).
The Core ledger routes it uses are live on staging (35/35 Developer operations match).
top_10_technically_interesting_features.status_detail: Client runs locally (CLI unpublished, npm E404). Backend routes are on staging. Not production.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.visual_demonstration: Split-screen terminal. Session A: an agent works and makes two architectural decisions; trigger /compact or end the session. Session B, fresh: the first thing on screen is the injected 'work state' block listing the objective, decisions, open items and what was not shown, and the agent continues without re-exploring. Cut to Console > Runs, where the CLI session run is classified 'cli-session' with its checkpoint as the outcome. Optional beat: stop Core and start a session to show the 'NOT RESTORED' notice and that the editor still works.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Credential-less, per-request multi-tenant MCP server
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: HTTP: `node dist/index.js` -> createHttpServer (http/app.ts), POST /mcp and GET /healthz on :3333. Stdio: `navis-mcp-stdio` (dist/stdio.js).
implementation_flow: The credential is read from IncomingMessage.rawHeaders by the shared @navis/identity reader, which refuses ambiguous or repeated credentials. With no credential the caller gets a plain HTTP 401 and no MCP server is constructed.
The credential is verified against Core GET /api/v1/developer/me, yielding an McpPrincipal (org, kind, permissions, capabilities). The server holds no Navis key of its own.
createMcpHandler's factory builds a fresh McpServer and NavisApiClient bound to that caller for every request (server.ts), so no state outlives a request.
The request id is generated server-side, never read from the caller, and returned as x-navis-request-id.

On a tool call, authorize() runs as refuse-only: permission 403 first, then capability 402. If it doesn't refuse, the call goes to the Developer API with the caller's credential, then through response bounds, error translation into a tool error that names the missing permission, and a telemetry record.
All 20 tools are annotated readOnlyHint. Server instructions steer models to navis_get_relevant_context first and to navis_me when refused.
evidence: request-context.ts header: 'THIS SERVER HOLDS NO NAVIS CREDENTIAL'.
server.ts header: 'One server per request, per caller'.
authorize.ts: 'authorize returns a refusal or nothing. There is no code path in which it grants access'.
tools/catalog.ts: 20 entries, each with an upstream route, permission and capability.
http/app.ts: MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1_000_000; both protocol eras via legacy:'stateless'.
~180 test cases in 12 files (http/app.test.ts 987 lines, identity-cost.test.ts, catalog.test.ts); sdks/integration/test_mcp_live.py (opt-in live).
Prior result, not re-run today: the 2026-09-28 audit measured 0/12 cross-org isolation breaches with two real orgs.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.status_detail: Runs locally on :3333 and over stdio. mcp.navislabs.in has no DNS. Upstream Developer API is on staging.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.visual_demonstration: Two terminals, two orgs' keys, the same question to the same MCP server, two different and isolated answers. Then a narrowly scoped key calls a tool, gets a refusal naming the exact permission, and the agent calls navis_me, which explains why. Overlay the per-request 'new server, new client' as an animated lifecycle diagram.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Task-aware organizational context (one primitive, one implementation)
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: MCP tool navis_get_relevant_context({task}) / SDK taskContext / CLI SessionStart with NAVIS_WORKSTATE_CONTEXT=1, all ending in POST /api/v1/developer/context
implementation_flow: The agent states its task in its own words; the api-client POSTs {task, since, until, token_budget}.
Core chain: credential -> principal (org from the api_keys/membership row) -> require_permission(view_memory) 403 -> require_capability(memory) 402 -> per-org rate limit 429.
The Developer route delegates to the SAME handler coroutine the web app uses, so the agent and the founder dashboard cannot disagree about the organization's context.
State, reasoning, intelligence and learning layers are filtered per credential and reported as withheld rather than refused, so a narrow key gets a smaller bundle instead of an opaque 403.
The response is mapped to a ContextBundle with freshness and sources, and the model is instructed to cite it rather than assert.
evidence: catalog.ts comment: 'view_memory + memory is the FLOOR ... filtered per credential inside the response and reported as withheld'.
Backend router.py docstring: 'exactly ONE implementation of each read, so the Developer API and the web app cannot disagree'.
Staging: GET /api/v1/developer/context -> 401 anonymous; POST operation present in the staging OpenAPI.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.status_detail: Backend on staging; clients local. Latency is the main risk: hook.ts records 20.8 s for this call on a cold local Core (2026-09-17). Prior notes (2026-09-25) recorded ~3.4 s after Core fixes that were then uncommitted.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.visual_demonstration: In Claude Code or Cursor, ask a task that depends on company facts ('prepare the renewal email for our largest customer'). Show the tool call, then the returned context with sources and freshness, then the agent's answer citing those sources. Pre-warm or cut around the latency. Use a curated demo org: the 2026-09-28 audit saw a ~61 KB response with raw third-party emails for a real org.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Agent execution ledger with official TypeScript and Python SDKs
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: `new Navis({ apiKey })` (TS) or the Python `navis` client, then tasks.create -> runs.start -> runs.recordStep -> runs.recordOutcome -> runs.finish
implementation_flow: me() returns principal.agentId and permissions; the example refuses unless the key is an agent key holding record_agent_runs, a write permission deliberately separate from view_observation.
POST /developer/agents/{id}/tasks with an idempotencyKey, then POST /developer/tasks/{id}/runs with a correlationId.

POST /runs/{id}/steps for typed steps: context_fetch, tool_call (tool name and kind, request and response metadata), model_generation (provider, model, input/output/cached tokens, costMicros, costBasis estimated vs reported, latency).
PUT /runs/{id}/outcome, then PATCH /runs/{id} to finish. GET /runs/{id}/telemetry returns the server-side rollup.
Transport adds retries, timeouts, request telemetry with templated paths (no ids leak into metrics), and one named error per refusal (NavisPermissionError, NavisPlanError, NavisConflictError...).
evidence: packages/sdk/src/index.ts: 'Nothing here is a mock, a fixture or a fallback'.
examples/typescript/execution.ts records context_fetch, tool_call and model_generation steps with token and cost fields.
Python SDK has one runtime dependency (httpx) and is MIT; the TS SDK is UNLICENSED.
Tests: sdk ~61, api-client ~70, python ~97, live integration ~27 (opt-in).
Prior result, not re-run today: on 2026-09-27 both SDKs were verified as packed external consumers against a real Core.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.status_detail: Unpublished (npm E404, PyPI 404). Backend ledger on staging.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.visual_demonstration: A 30-line script in an editor runs; each step lands live as a row in Console > Runs > Run detail, building a timeline: context fetch, tool call (17 matches), model generation (tokens, cost). The same script in Python produces an identical run.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Outcome economics and the run story
implementation_flow: loadDeveloper builds a fresh API client per request from the session cookie with cache no-store; pages are force-dynamic so no tenant's data is ever served from a shared cache.
GET /developer/economics: Core recomputes from run, step and outcome rows (no economics table). context_fetched is the presence of a context_fetch step, and groups are task x used-context.
Cost per successful outcome = spend over all attempts / successes, so retries are not hidden.
The panel renders absence as '—' using a Number.isFinite guard (null, NaN and Infinity never reach a cost column).

The run page fetches telemetry, steps (limit 200), agents and tasks in parallel. classifyRun labels it activity, cli-session or no-activity, and run-story.ts writes each sentence strictly from a field ('not reported', never 'not used' or zero).
evidence: EconomicsPanel.tsx header: 'DERIVED, NOT STORED' and 'NULL IS RENDERED AS ABSENCE, NEVER AS ZERO'.
run-story.ts: 'EVERY STATEMENT HERE IS A READING OF A FIELD'.
Tests: EconomicsPanel.test.tsx, RunStory.test.tsx, RunTable.test.tsx, RunDetailPanel.test.ts.
Backend run_service.py:228-231 context_fetched derived from context_fetch steps.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.status_detail: Console local only; economics route on staging. Needs real successful runs in both with-context and without-context groups to be meaningful. Prior notes: there is no synthetic-run marker, so harness runs cannot be filtered out.
top_10_technically_interesting_features.visual_demonstration: The money shot only if the data is real: a two-column comparison of cost per successful outcome with vs without Navis context for the same task. Then drill into one run and let the narrative sentences type out. Do not seed numbers for the camera.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Contract-locked platform: OpenAPI as the single source for SDKs, docs and agents
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: `npm run contract:check` and `npm run docs:generate` in CI; GET /llms.txt and /SKILL.md on the console
implementation_flow: A normalised OpenAPI snapshot of the Core is committed as contracts/openapi/developer.json.

contract.ts lists every SDK route. The test asserts each exists in the spec and that every /developer operation is either covered or listed in EXCLUDED with a reason, so a new route without an SDK method fails the build.

The generators render the API reference and docs data; CI runs them and fails on any git diff.
The console serves agent-facing /llms.txt and /SKILL.md, which state when no MCP endpoint is configured rather than printing a dead URL.
evidence: ci.yml steps 'Contract is normalized' and 'Generated docs match the contract'.
Staging OpenAPI diff on 2026-10-04: 35/35 Developer operations identical to the repo contract.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Human-approved real-world execution with a truthful send-state
files: Navis-AI/src/services/api.ts (proposeActions 4375, requestAction 4400, approveExecution 4429, retryExecution 4445, get/save/regenerateActionDraft 4464-4492, rejectExecution 4502, cancelExecution 4510)
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: /dashboard/actions (Action Center) and the action proposals in Today and Ask Navis
implementation_flow: A decision or brief proposes an action (POST /brief/propose-actions or /actions), creating an ExecutionRequest in status 'requested'.

executionAdapter.ts maps wire statuses to Kanban lanes (requested->proposed, approved, executing, executed, failed, rejected/cancelled->ignored), surfacing wire fields as evidence rather than inventing values.
DraftReviewPanel reads, saves and regenerates the draft through /actions/{id}/draft.
A human POSTs /actions/{id}/approve. There is no auto path: actionPolicies.ts documents that the Core only drains APPROVED rows.

The Celery worker runs production_providers with real senders: Gmail send and reply, Calendar create/reschedule/cancel, Slack chat.postMessage via the org's own grants. _production_safe withholds any provider that would dry-run.

describeSend (executionStatus.ts) says 'sent' only when provider_reference carries a real external id. A dryrun- id or dry_run flag means 'dry_run'; approved/executing means 'sending', never 'sent'. Retry is offered only when Core would accept it (max 5 attempts), and OAuth failures map to 'reconnect'.
evidence: actionPolicies.ts create_meeting comment: 'There is no auto-execution path on the backend'.
executionStatus.ts readProviderReference: 'not null is NOT proof of a send. Only a non-empty external_id is'.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Ask Navis: multi-turn command chat over the organization
top_10_technically_interesting_features.entry_point: /dashboard/ask and the AskNavisMini widget on Today
implementation_flow: askOrchestrator issues ONE request through askNavis; it no longer simulates a reasoning pipeline (the removed 11-stage fake telemetry is documented in its header).
POST /chat body: question (trimmed to 2,000 chars), active_signal_id, thread_id, time_zone, and the last 6 recent_turns.

Multi-turn continuations echo state from the previous assistant turn: pending_scheduling (sent even when all-null, because Core routes on its presence), pending_calendar_event_id and pending_email, so 'tomorrow at 3' completes the pending flow.
The response carries intent, citations and actionProposals. A proposal with an execution_id is a real ExecutionRequest (isExecutableProposal) and is approved via feature 7.
Local classifyIntent and extractEntities are used only as UI fallbacks and are never presented as backend work.

top_10_technically_interesting_features.name: Daily brief and the five-stage decision lifecycle
files: src/services/api.ts (getContextBundle 2019, getBriefToday 4303, generateBrief 4308, getDecisionHistory, getLearningSummary, getOutcomes)
implementation_flow: Today reads GET /brief/today (ranked decisions and obligations) and GET /context, adapting the ScopedView's entities into attention items and counts into memory state (adaptScopedViewToBundle). /decide is not a Core route; the top decision is brief.decisions[0].
/context deliberately uses fetchJson, not fetchJsonOr, so a failed read renders an error state instead of a reassuring 'nothing needs you'.
briefingComposer, obligations and decisionExplanation turn wire fields into cards with evidence and explanations.

The Decisions page reads /brief/decisions/history, /learning/summary and /outcomes and renders each decision through STAGE_ORDER (decision, your call, execution, outcome, learning), keeping fact, pending and not-applicable visually distinct.

cinematic_launch_video_top_3.feature_ref: top_10 #3 Task-aware context, delivered by #2 the multi-tenant MCP server
cinematic_launch_video_top_3.working_title: Ask your company, from inside your agent
cinematic_launch_video_top_3.why_strongest: It is the core value proposition in one gesture: any MCP agent asks a task-shaped question and gets cited, permission-scoped organizational context. The isolation and refusal beats show it is enterprise-grade, not a demo.
shot_list: In Cursor or Claude Code: 'Draft the renewal note for our biggest customer.'
Tool call navis_get_relevant_context fires; the context panel shows sources and freshness.
The answer cites the sources instead of guessing.
Split screen: a second org's key asks the same question and gets that org's answer, not the first one's.
A read-only key tries a gated tool, gets a refusal naming the permission, and navis_me explains it.
prerequisites: A curated demo organization with clean, non-sensitive data. A real org's response was ~61 KB with raw third-party emails on 2026-09-28.
The MCP server running (:3333 or stdio) against staging or local Core.
Latency handled: pre-warm or edit around a multi-second context call.
honesty_guardrails: The tools are read-only; the agent cannot change org data through MCP.
Do not show a hosted MCP URL; mcp.navislabs.in does not exist.

cinematic_launch_video_top_3.why_strongest: The most visual payoff: a decision becomes a real email in a real inbox and a real calendar invite, with the human visibly in control and the UI refusing to claim 'sent' until Gmail confirms.
